provenance.public_window: The hillclimb changed only dead_min_run, dead_trim, dead_close, dead_lead_cut, dead_out_lead_cut, dead_outside_m, dead_still_mps, dead_still_frames, dead_pace_still_mps, handover_lag, spell_flip_p, spell_flip_frames, spell_flip_seen, spell_logit, switch_penalty, spell_push_mps, spell_push_frames, spell_push_unseen and the emission's q_logit_a, q_logit_dist and q_logit_margin. It scored files on the public window as a correctness check, never inside a selection rule: tier0_v2, tier0_v7 and tier0_v0 at 09:32 and 09:36 IST on 2026-10-24, and tier0_v8 at 11:40 IST. Every experiment from E17 on, selection rules v3 and v4, spell_merge_frames, the spell_push fields, switch_penalty and the spell_flip and dead_lead fields came after the first read. Inherited from tier0_v1: Selection read only the Metrica dev worlds in sweep_worlds. The marginal temper grid {0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2} was set from a public-window smoke test that put temper's useful range at 0.01 to 0.1. The m2 worlds merge Metrica spells under 2 s because raw Metrica spells are much shorter than the public window's, though 2 s was not fitted to the window. The decoder dead_bias 1.0 was selected from a {1, 3} axis whose 1.0 is the flat default, argued partly from a public-window count. These choices were committed on 2026-10-21. EVALUATION.md had said since 2026-09-24 to use the window to check correctness and never to choose between two versions. Upstream f8f2629 (2026-10-23) made RULES.md say the window is not training data and not a tuning set. v1 won this sweep on dev but was set aside the same day, on CHALLENGE.md and public-window figures (23 predicted possessions against 17, spellF1 0.310 against 0.412). On controlled-possession dev worlds it later lost to v0 at 5 s (-0.026 spellF1) and tied at 3 s. This public_window text was added by hand on 2026-10-24, and the command above does not write it. See possession/DESIGN.md, Measurements and constant provenance.
provenance.selection: Pre-registered rule v2 (.audit/hillclimb-2026-10-24.tsv): candidates are v1's chain with dead_min_run {101, 126} x dead_trim {0, 12, 25, 37, 50} x dead_close {0, 100, 150, 200, 300}. Synthetic groups (Metrica m0, h1p3, h3p3 and IDSSE m0, m2 at generator dead_bias 1, 2.6, 4, seeds 0-4) only veto: a candidate's seed-mean pooled spellF1 margin over baseline_smooth50 must be at least the incumbent 101/50/0's minus 0.003 in every group, because the renewal generator switches masks at label boundaries. The minimum over native PFF m0 and m2 on odd-indexed games ranks; ties within 0.003 go to the higher synthetic minimum. Even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. Game indices count from 1: the odd-indexed games are pff.GAMES[0::2]. dead_outside_m was added after the dead rule, judged on native PFF only: it had to raise both odd-game margins and keep a 90% per-game lower bound above 0 on even games. The q_logit terms come from pre-registered experiment E5: logit(q) = a + b ln(1 + nearest_m) + c ln(1 + min(margin_m, 30)), a logistic fit of P(token == labelled team) on the frames PFF's tracker saw in live play on the odd-indexed games (probes.py fit_logit, 1,869,449 frames). The fitted emission replaced the constant q at v1's temper after passing the synthetic veto (at least tier0_v3's margin minus 0.003 in every group) and ranking first on the odd-game PFF minimum among tempers {0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2}; even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. handover_lag comes from pre-registered experiment E7: matched dev possessions showed the hand-overs between the teams 10 to 22 frames early on every label source (median, probes.py spells), because the nearest-team token flips while a pass is in the air. Candidates were lag {0, 5, ..., 30} crossed with a snap to the receiver's first frame within {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3} m; the synthetic veto (at least tier0_v4's margin minus 0.003 in every group) and the odd-game PFF minimum chose lag 15, the smallest change within 0.003 of the best; even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. dead_still_mps and dead_still_frames come from pre-registered experiment E11: on frames PFF's tracker saw in the odd-indexed games, a ball under 1 m/s inside a slow run of 50-100 frames is dead 87% of the time and 98% beyond 100 (probes.py still). Candidates were 0.5 or 1 m/s over 25, 50 or 100 frames; all passed the synthetic veto (at least tier0_v5's margin minus 0.003 in every group), and the odd-game PFF minimum with the tie rule (within 0.003, the longer run first) chose 1 m/s over 50 frames; even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. dead_pace_still_mps comes from pre-registered experiment E13: on the odd-indexed PFF games, frames whose median player speed is under 0.5 m/s are dead 94% of the time (probes.py motion). Candidates crossed a live override {off, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3} m/s with a still threshold {off, 0.5, 0.75} m/s; every live override lost, and the odd-game PFF minimum with the tie rule (within 0.003, the smaller still threshold first) chose 0.5 m/s alone; even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. spell_push_mps, spell_push_frames and spell_push_unseen come from pre-registered experiments E25 and E26: after the dead-run rule and before the merge and the lag, a possession shorter than spell_push_frames whose frames are at least spell_push_unseen without a token, and whose mean push toward its own team (median player x velocity toward the goal it attacks, home minus away) is at most -spell_push_mps, goes to the other team (decoder._push_flip). E25 judged every short possession and was vetoed on IDSSE m0. E26, designed after that veto, added the no-token gate on the inference (never measured) that push trails a turnover, over gates {0.5, 0.8} x (2 m/s, 125 frames), (2, 250), (3, 250), the points E25 ranked highest. Rule v2 (synthetic veto at tier0_v7 minus 0.003 in every group; the odd-game minimum over PFF m0 and m2 ranks; ties within 0.003 to the base, then the fewest changed fields, then the higher minimum) chose 2 m/s over 250 frames at 0.5, by 0.00004 over 3 m/s; even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. The gate makes the stage fire rarely in the synthetic worlds, so the veto says little about per-touch labels. No StatsBomb data entered this selection. switch_penalty comes from pre-registered experiment E27 on tier0_v9: the chain's block posterior is decoded by the label path that maximises the summed log posterior minus switch_penalty per change of team (decoder._penalized_path), so an island of one team inside the other survives only when its summed block log-odds reach twice the penalty. A design fan-out proposed 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32, with a waiver at dead frames for 8 and 16; the registrant added 1 ahead of them before any result, because temper 0.1 flattens the posterior. Rule v2 (synthetic veto at tier0_v9 minus 0.003 in every group; the odd-game minimum over PFF m0 and m2 ranks; ties within 0.003 to the base, then the smaller penalty) chose 1, the only candidate the IDSSE m0 groups did not veto (2 missed by 0.0010); even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. The fan-out's own kill gate, that posterior confidence separate matched from unmatched short possessions by 0.10 beyond length, was demoted to a diagnostic before any result and then failed (0.04 and 0.06), so under the fan-out's registration the result would be no change, and the penalty acts as a cut of the shortest weak islands. No StatsBomb data entered this selection. spell_flip_p and spell_logit come from pre-registered experiment E29 on tier0_v10. A label-reading oracle (probes.py flipruns) put the ceiling of giving short possessions to the other team at +0.041 on PFF-A m0 for runs with a token on half their frames or more. A ridge-1 Newton logistic over decoder.SPELL_FEATURES (label-free: length, token shares, closest own approach, ball speed, own margin, push, the chain's log-odds and the neighbours) was fitted on the PFF-A m0 labels (pff.GAMES[0::2]) to say when giving one short possession away alone raises the half's matched possessions minus F/2 per predicted spell; the weights are that fit on all A games, rounded to 4 places. Candidates, registered before the first gate: base and token share 0.5+ or all runs at P 0.8, 0.65 and 0.5, ranked on 2-fold game-OOF PFF-A margins; the tie order (higher cut first, token-gated before all) was fixed after the first-gate numbers by structure. Rule v2 (synthetic veto at tier0_v10 minus 0.003 in every group with the all-A weights; the odd-game OOF minimum over PFF m0 and m2 ranks; ties within 0.003 to the base, then the tie order) chose token share 0.5+ at P 0.8; the 0.65 and 0.5 cuts failed the IDSSE m0 groups. Even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. The weights are PFF-derived numbers. No StatsBomb data entered this selection. E30 refitted the same model with the token-share feature left out (its weight 0) after tier0_v11, the E29 winner, passed PFF-B and seeds 15-24 and was then stopped by its registered BAR-ATH check: the median token share of BAR-ATH's short runs (1.000) sat above PFF-A's 90th percentile (0.946). That design used a label-free match-wide BAR-ATH statistic, under the team's unconfirmed reading of RULES.md; the weights are still fitted only on PFF-A labels. Same arms, tie order and rule v2 chose token share 0.5+ at P 0.8 again, and the BAR-ATH check, over the features with a non-zero weight, passed before this file was frozen. That pass was certain once the one feature outside PFF-A's range was left out, because the check's medians do not depend on the weights, so it is no evidence of transfer. dead_lead_cut and dead_out_lead_cut come from pre-registered experiment E32 on tier0_v12. Label-reading oracles on PFF-A (probes.py deadedges, deadstarts) put +0.021 at the start edges of stoppages the dead rule already marks, because dead_trim cuts every dead run's start; where the ball is seen more than dead_outside_m outside the pitch near the run's start, the cue starts a median 5 frames before the labelled stoppage. Candidates, registered before any result: out-only cuts 25, 40, 50 and lead cuts 10 to 50 with out variants (probes.py LEAD_GRID). Rule v2 (synthetic veto at tier0_v12 minus 0.003 in every group; the odd-game minimum over PFF m0 and m2 ranks; ties within 0.003 to the base, then the registered order: out-only cuts smallest first, then lead cuts 10 to 50, each plain before its out variants) chose this file's values. Even-indexed PFF games and seeds 15-24 only confirm. No BAR-ATH statistic was read. No StatsBomb data entered this selection.
